payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Given the inventory and nested boundary map, does independent inspection establish completed stuffing, affirmative incompleteness, or unresolved completion, and what requested progress is actually established?
node.criteria: Pass only when established paper-and-cup identity and concrete entry, containment, or compression establish completed stuffing; some paper may remain outside. Fail when affirmative geometry establishes incomplete insertion, wholly external placement, rim-only placement without stuffing, or adequately visible absence of a required object. Report whether this failure accompanies positive requested insertion progress or established no progress. Unknown when completion requires an unresolved spatial relation or receiver identity, or when established entry cannot be distinguished as intermediate versus completed stuffing. A boundary-mapping pass is not positive entry evidence. Unresolved source correspondence alone does not invalidate established spatial evidence, but an unresolved edited receiver identity prevents claiming insertion into a cup.
node.binding: Consume s1 and s4_opening_entry in saved order as context, then inspect the edited image independently. Read the nested check's typed identity, geometry, progress, and completion findings rather than treating its execution status as their truth value. Revisit specifically localized hidden paper segments and test whether visible containment, compression, or boundary continuity settles stuffing extent. Resolve conflicts only with explicit visible evidence. Do not promote a mapping pass to entry, an entry finding to completion, or completion failure to no progress. Preserve genuine hidden-entry uncertainty; do not infer missing visual facts from the instruction, source cup, hand grip, or altered printing.

dependencies.evidence: Source: a large white sheet of paper is visible beside a blue cup lying on its side; the cup has a broad oval opening and enclosing walls. Edited: a blue printed paper/card is held in front of a reddish rounded object with a dark curved line. The paper’s outline is mostly visible, though its upper edge is partly overlapped by the hand; the reddish object is partly obscured by the paper and hand, and its visible contour does not clearly establish a cup. Direct comparison does not establish that the edited reddish object corresponds to the source cup. The images allow a grounded inventory, but edited cup identity and source-to-edit correspondence remain unresolved.

Boundary map: The blue printed paper/card has a visible pointed upper-right corner, a slanted right edge, a lower-right corner, a curved lower edge, and a lower-left point; its left/upper-left boundary is partly covered by the hand and fingers. The hand overlaps the paper’s upper-left area. The paper’s right edge and lower portion lie in front of the reddish rounded object, whose visible contour and dark curved line do not establish a cup opening or enclosing cup walls. No paper segment is visibly disappearing behind a receiver boundary; the hand obscures only the paper’s upper-left region, not a demonstrated contact with the reddish object. No alternative receiver is established. Receiver identity: unresolved. Geometry: established wholly external placement—the visible paper is in front of the object, and its visible outline does not enter it. Requested progress: excluded. Completion: excluded.
